name: Abbott Diabetes Care
products: FreeStyle Libre 2, Libre 3, Libre 3 Plus, Lingo (enzymatic, 14-15 day wear)
contact_emails: adc_iis@abbott.com (Investigator-Initiated Studies); abbottcorporate@abbott.com; karen.twiggmay@abbott.com (media); ADChelpuk@abbott.com (UK support)
why_relevant: Global market leader, and Sugar-Sugar already ingests the Libre export format. Standard support channels are automated and filtered - the IIS route is the only viable academic path.
suggested_ask: Submit an Investigator-Initiated Study proposal to adc_iis@abbott.com framed as measuring how Libre users interpret rate-of-change trend arrows. Non-financial support (sensors, anonymised data) is reviewed continuously; financial grants close 15 September annually.
notes: Needs a Declaration of Eligibility, a structured Study Proposal Form and an investigator CV. Sugar-Sugar ALREADY supports the Libre format, so lead with participant recruitment and export validation, not "please integrate your CGM". NEVER approach Abbott, Dexcom and Medtronic as one consortium - Abbott manufactures the Instinct CGM for MiniMed while competing with Medtronic in standalone CGM.

name: Dexcom, Inc.
products: Dexcom G6, G7, ONE/ONE+, Stelo (enzymatic, 10-15.5 day wear)
why_relevant: The easiest technical path of the big three: developer.dexcom.com grants instant sandbox credentials with no corporate pre-approval. Dexcom enforces a retrospective delay on glucose values (1h US, 3h international) to stop real-time third-party dosing - Sugar-Sugar evaluates retrospective traces, so it sits inside that framework rather than against it.
suggested_ask: Register an academic developer org for sandbox credentials and build the Dexcom parser; in parallel email clinicalresearch@dexcom.com citing the Rostock ethics clearance.
notes: Three tiers: sandbox, self-service Limited Access (5 production users), Full Access requiring a partnership questionnaire and data licensing agreement. Already a supported format in Sugar-Sugar - lead with recruitment and export validation. Dexcom 2025 reporting continued to identify Abbott-related patent litigation, so keep the invitation strictly bilateral.

name: Medtronic Diabetes
products: Guardian Sensor 3/4, Simplera, MiniMed 780G AID (enzymatic, 7-day wear)
portals: medtronicdiabetes.com; ISR intake via practice management
why_relevant: The most centralised of the three. Integrations are restricted to formal corporate alliances or regulated trials, so this is a long game.
suggested_ask: Investigator-Sponsored Research proposal positioning Sugar-Sugar as a behavioural benchmark: human forecasting error against the MiniMed 780G predictive Auto-Basal algorithm. Ask ONLY for the CGM trace and data-export layer unless pump/AID data become methodologically necessary.
notes: Already a supported format. Keep the invitation bilateral and identical in terms to the Abbott and Dexcom ones.

name: Roche Diabetes Care
products: Accu-Chek SmartGuide, mySugr ecosystem (enzymatic, 14-day wear)
why_relevant: The sharpest strategic fit of any manufacturer. Their SmartGuide Predict app (built with IBM) forecasts glucose trends with ML - which is precisely the thing Sugar-Sugar establishes a human baseline for.
suggested_ask: Exploratory digital-health approach through media and innovation channels. Pitch the synergy with SmartGuide Predict, but state explicitly that Sugar-Sugar measures HUMAN prediction and is not evaluating or benchmarking their proprietary algorithm - the second report is emphatic that these must be separated in writing.
notes: Roche also has a Romanian arm (accu-chek.ro) worth pairing with the Romanian outreach.

name: Senseonics Holdings
products: Eversense E3, Eversense 365 (implantable optical fluorescence, 180-365 day wear)
why_relevant: Fully implantable long-wear sensors. They actively support real-world evidence studies that show off longitudinal data stability - a 180-365 day trace is a different prediction problem from a 14-day one.
suggested_ask: Contact Senseonics DIRECTLY. Do not route through Ascensia.
notes: CORRECTION from the second report: Ascensia is no longer the gatekeeper. Ascensia historically commercialised Eversense but those functions transitioned back to Senseonics in January 2026. The first report still described them as "partnered with Ascensia" - that is out of date.

name: Sibionics (Shenzhen Silicon-based Intelligent Tech)
products: SIBIONICS GS1, SiJoy, CKM (enzymatic, 14-day factory calibrated)
why_relevant: The single most accessible manufacturer in this file, and the only one running a standing Research Fund that explicitly invites bioengineers, clinical researchers and AI scientists to apply for in-kind sensor grants. The fund is scoped at CGM data plus digital health platforms and AI predictive algorithms - which is Sugar-Sugar described back to us.
suggested_ask: Apply to the Research Fund with a structured abstract requesting in-kind GS1 sensors, to compare human forecasting accuracy against their embedded AI predictive engine. Reviewed by a three-person expert panel.
notes: The two reports disagree on sequencing: the first puts Sibionics in the very first wave because of the open Research Fund and free hardware; the second puts it in the second wave, ranking by reach instead. Both are defensible - the fund is the cheapest possible first move, so it costs little to do both.

name: Sinocare Inc.
products: iCan i3, iCan i6 (enzymatic, 15-day wear)
why_relevant: Large public diagnostics manufacturer scaling the iCan CGM internationally and responsive to outside developers.
suggested_ask: Open a channel on standardised CSV and API data ingest for iCan devices, so Sugar-Sugar can read their exports.
notes: Named in the second report as a FIRST-wave target, on the strength of direct international email access plus fast-expanding clinical and regulatory activity. Coordinate European recruitment with A. Menarini Diagnostics, which holds exclusive reimbursed-market rights in parts of Europe.

name: i-SENS, Inc.
products: CareSens Air (enzymatic, 15-day wear, factory calibrated)
why_relevant: Korean market leader expanding across Europe, with published direct executive contacts for the team that owns CareSens Air API interoperability.
suggested_ask: Contact Business Innovation directly about CareSens Air data ingest into Sugar-Sugar.
notes: Named executive emails are published - unusually open for a manufacturer.

name: Medtrum Technologies
products: TouchCare Nano CGM, TouchCare patch pump (enzymatic, 14-day wear)
contact_emails: info.uk@medtrum.co.uk; info.germany@medtrum.com; info.france@medtrum.fr; info@medtrum.nl; info.denmark@medtrum.com; kundsupport@medtrum.se; info@medtrum.com.hk; info@medtrum.com
why_relevant: Explicitly collaborative toward the open-source diabetes data community, including Nightscout and AndroidAPS integrations - the same crowd as the Telegram and Facebook loop rooms already in this registry.
suggested_ask: Work with the UK/Germany offices on a parser for TouchCare and EasyPatch cloud exports, alongside the open-source community.
notes: Decentralised European subsidiaries mean a national office answers faster than head office - the second report lists eight affiliate mailboxes.

name: MicroTech Medical
products: AiDEX, LinX CGM, LinX M1/S1 (enzymatic, 14-day wear)
why_relevant: Publishes public API documentation for AiDEX, which makes a parser cheap to build.
suggested_ask: Request API access and sample traces for AiDEX.
notes: A LinX CGM user group already exists on Facebook and is in the Facebook catalogue. GlucoRx AiDEX is a RETAIL REBRAND of the MicroTech platform, not a separate manufacturer - do not double-count it.

name: Jiangsu Yuwell Medical Equipment
products: Anytrans CGM, CT3 (enzymatic, 14-day wear)
why_relevant: Large diversified conglomerate; the CGM R&D division sits behind the international trade division.
suggested_ask: Low priority. Route through overseas@yuwell.com and expect to be redirected.
notes: Retail rebranding is common here - identify the underlying manufacturer and file format rather than chasing a corporate endorsement.

name: Zhejiang POCTech Co.
products: CT-100, POCTech CGM (enzymatic, 7-14 day wear)
why_relevant: Lean specialist sensor developer with no developer portal.
suggested_ask: Direct sales or management mailbox, or meet them at ADA/EASD.
notes: Conference contact may work better than email.

name: DiaMonTech AG
products: D-Pocket, D-Sensor (mid-infrared photothermal spectroscopy, non-invasive)
why_relevant: Non-invasive sensing venture with a flat structure - mail sent to the corporate inbox is read by the founders, CMO or VP Clinical Affairs within days. These companies have a strong commercial incentive to join independent benchmarking, because non-invasive optical, radiofrequency and microneedle systems must keep proving accuracy against enzymatic gold standards. German deep-tech, which pairs with the Rostock affiliation.
suggested_ask: Offer to benchmark their prototype sensor traces against standard enzymatic traces inside the Sugar-Sugar interface.
notes: German company plus German ethics approval is a natural opening line.

Actively seeks clinical trial participants, academic evaluation and research collaborations.
suggested_ask: Benchmarking offer, same framing as DiaMonTech.

name: PKvitality
products: K'Watch Glucose (microneedle continuous interstitial fluid sensor)
why_relevant: Non-invasive sensing venture with a flat structure - mail sent to the corporate inbox is read by the founders, CMO or VP Clinical Affairs within days. These companies have a strong commercial incentive to join independent benchmarking, because non-invasive optical, radiofrequency and microneedle systems must keep proving accuracy against enzymatic gold standards. EU Horizon EIC Accelerator funded and described as highly receptive to digital health benchmarking - and an EU grant history makes a joint European proposal plausible.

name: Nemaura Medical, Inc.
products: sugarBEAT, proBEAT (transdermal reverse iontophoresis patch, daily non-invasive)
why_relevant: Non-invasive sensing venture with a flat structure - mail sent to the corporate inbox is read by the founders, CMO or VP Clinical Affairs within days. These companies have a strong commercial incentive to join independent benchmarking, because non-invasive optical, radiofrequency and microneedle systems must keep proving accuracy against enzymatic gold standards. Open direct executive and investor contact routes, and actively seeking third-party validation studies.
suggested_ask: Direct approach to investor relations offering independent validation.
notes: Contact routes are investor-relations rather than clinical - pitch the validation value.

name: Infinovo Medical (Glunovo)
products: Glunovo D3 / p3 CGM systems and associated apps and data-sharing tools
portals: Infinovo Medical on LinkedIn and Facebook
why_relevant: Named in the second report as a second-wave target. Glunovo has appeared in recent clinical research including randomised and residual-bound accuracy studies, which makes their traces scientifically interesting rather than just another format.
suggested_ask: Multiple human-routable emails - start with info@infinovo.com and ask about export format and a de-identified sample file.
notes: Second report only. Distributor availability varies by country and no global exclusivity was identified, so approach the company directly.

name: Biolinq, Inc.
products: Biolinq Shine - intradermal glucose-sensor patch with an integrated visual display, no phone required. FDA De Novo classification September 2025
contact_emails: Not published. Route through company leadership or management.
why_relevant: High strategic relevance despite tiny share. Positioned at metabolic health and non-insulin users, which overlaps the broader population interested in glucose prediction - the same non-diabetic arm the study recruits. A display-on-patch device also changes what a user sees, which is directly relevant to a study about human forecasting.
suggested_ask: Ask about future data export. Expect launch-execution focus and controlled messaging, so keep the request small.
notes: Second report only. No direct contact email published - this is the main obstacle. No website or contact email was given in either source report - find the official site before contacting.

name: Glucotrack, Inc.
products: Continuous blood-glucose monitoring system designed for multi-year operation (long-duration implantable)
why_relevant: Not commercially distributed, so no recruitment value. Relevant only as a long-duration implantable question alongside Senseonics, and development-stage data may be confidential.
suggested_ask: Ask to be routed to clinical or scientific leadership. Realistically a future extension of the study, not this one.
notes: Second report only. Lowest priority in the file - listed so it is not rediscovered as a lead.
